alt.en: A sepia studio photograph on a card mount with rounded corners: five young women in long dresses and four young men in suits, some seated on chairs and a sofa, some standing, around a small round table in front of a column and a heavy curtain.
alt.es: Fotografía de estudio en sepia sobre un cartón de esquinas redondeadas: cinco mujeres jóvenes con vestidos largos y cuatro hombres jóvenes de traje, unos sentados en sillas y un sofá y otros de pie, alrededor de una mesita redonda, delante de una columna y una cortina gruesa.

caption.en: Fisk University's Jubilee Singers in a carte de visite of the 1870s, named in the Library of Congress record as Minnie Tate, Greene Evans, Isaac Dickerson, Jennie Jackson, Maggie Porter, Ella Sheppard, Thomas Rutling, Benjamin Holmes and Eliza Walker: the company whose songs, Steal Away among them, were printed as Jubilee Songs in 1872.
caption.es: Los Jubilee Singers de la Universidad Fisk en una carte de visite de la década de 1870, que el registro de la Biblioteca del Congreso nombra como Minnie Tate, Greene Evans, Isaac Dickerson, Jennie Jackson, Maggie Porter, Ella Sheppard, Thomas Rutling, Benjamin Holmes y Eliza Walker: el grupo cuyas canciones, Steal Away entre ellas, se imprimieron como Jubilee Songs en 1872.

source: Jubilee Singers, Fisk University, Nashville, Tenn. (carte de visite, albumen print; photographer attributed: James Wallace Black, 1825-1896; published by the American Missionary Association)
library: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Gladstone Collection of African American Photographs
licenceEvidence: Library of Congress catalogue record (https://lccn.loc.gov/2010647805/marcxml), rights field: "No known restrictions on publication." Photograph made 1870 to 1880; photographer James Wallace Black died 1896 (see rights.md).
credit: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, LC-DIG-ppmsca-11008

alt.en: A black-and-white photograph of a wide unpaved street with picket fences and young trees. At the far end stands a large brick building of several storeys with a tall pointed tower; on the right, a church tower with a steep spire and wooden houses with porches. One small, distant figure walks along the far pavement.
alt.es: Fotografía en blanco y negro de una calle ancha sin pavimentar, con cercas de estacas y árboles jóvenes. Al fondo se alza un gran edificio de ladrillo de varias plantas con una torre alta y puntiaguda; a la derecha, la torre de una iglesia con una aguja empinada y casas de madera con porche. Una figura pequeña y lejana camina por la acera del fondo.

caption.en: Fisk University in Nashville in about 1899, with Jubilee Hall at the end of the street: built in 1876, it was paid for with the money the Jubilee Singers raised on their tours, Fisk says.
caption.es: La Universidad Fisk, en Nashville, hacia 1899, con el Jubilee Hall al fondo de la calle: construido en 1876, se pagó con el dinero que reunieron los Jubilee Singers en sus giras, según la propia Fisk.

source: [Addison Avenue looking north at Fisk University, Nashville, Tennessee, showing Jubilee Hall, Fisk memorial chapel, and the Daniel Hand Model School] (photographic print), from the African American Photographs Assembled for the 1900 Paris Exposition
library: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
licenceEvidence: Library of Congress catalogue record (https://lccn.loc.gov/90712951/marcxml), rights field: "No known restrictions on publication." Photograph dated [1899?], photographer not named; exhibited Paris 1900 (see rights.md).
credit: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, LC-USZ62-100551

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "28 Jubilee Songs." and, in black-letter type, "Steal Away.", in four parts on two staves in 2/4 time with one flat, the refrain and the first two verses under the notes, marked "p", "f" and "D. C.", with verses 3 and 4 printed below.
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el encabezado "28 Jubilee Songs." y, en letra gótica, "Steal Away.", a cuatro voces en dos pentagramas, en 2/4 y con un bemol; bajo las notas, el estribillo y las dos primeras estrofas, con las indicaciones "p", "f" y "D. C.", y debajo las estrofas 3 y 4.

caption.en: Steal Away on page 28 of Jubilee Songs (New York, 1872), the Fisk singers' first book and the song's earliest known printing, with the words as George L. White took them down and the music as Theodore F. Seward wrote it down.
caption.es: Steal Away en la página 28 de Jubilee Songs (Nueva York, 1872), el primer libro de los cantantes de Fisk y la impresión más antigua que se conoce de la canción, con la letra anotada por George L. White y la música por Theodore F. Seward.

source: Jubilee Songs: As Sung by the Jubilee Singers of Fisk University (Nashville, Tenn.) under the Auspices of the American Missionary Association (New York: Biglow & Main, 1872), p. 28, "Steal Away."
library: Emory University, Manuscript, Archives and Rare Book Library (digitized for the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published New York 1872; Seward died 1902, White died 1895. Emory's record: "The online edition of this book in the public domain, i.e., not protected by copyright, has been produced by the Emory University Digital Library Publications Program" (https://archive.org/details/29208201.4853.emory.edu). Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: Emory University, Manuscript, Archives and Rare Book Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed book page headed "Welcome of the Singers to London. 33": a report of a concert, with the guests listed, that includes "Their first song was, 'Steal away to Jesus.' It was sung slowly; the first chords came floating on our senses like gentle fairy music".
alt.es: Página impresa de un libro con el encabezado "Welcome of the Singers to London. 33": la crónica de un concierto, con la lista de invitados, que incluye "Their first song was, 'Steal away to Jesus.' It was sung slowly; the first chords came floating on our senses like gentle fairy music".

caption.en: Page 33 of G. D. Pike's The Singing Campaign for Ten Thousand Pounds (New York, 1875), quoting a London music paper on the singers' first London concert, at Willis's Rooms on 6 May 1873: "Their first song was, 'Steal away to Jesus.'"
caption.es: Página 33 de The Singing Campaign for Ten Thousand Pounds, de G. D. Pike (Nueva York, 1875), que cita a una revista musical londinense sobre el primer concierto de los cantantes en Londres, en Willis's Rooms el 6 de mayo de 1873: "Their first song was, 'Steal away to Jesus.'" (Su primera canción fue «Steal away to Jesus»).

source: Gustavus D. Pike, The Singing Campaign for Ten Thousand Pounds; or, The Jubilee Singers in Great Britain, revised edition (New York: American Missionary Association, 1875), p. 33
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Title page: New York, American Missionary Association, 1875; "Entered, according to Act of Congress, in the year 1875, by The American Missionary Association". Author Gustavus D. Pike died 1885. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive
